boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Grinnell traditions spanning student films, playful competition, cultural showcases, campus milestones, creative expression, and annual community events.

cards.title: Cheer Grinnell’s Five-Minute Films
cards.subtitle: The student-made film festival at the Harris Center
cards.notes: Watch for the student committee’s event announcement, then secure admission early or create a short film for a future festival.
cards.short_summary: A homegrown festival turns student-made shorts into a shared exercise in Grinnell humor.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell identifies Titular Head as an annual student film festival featuring short films of up to five minutes made by students and consistently hosted by student committees since its 1989 reinvention.
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 virtual celebration is closed; consult the current College calendar for the next student festival.

cards.title: Race Beneath the Golden Helmet
cards.subtitle: A spring spoof staged on Mac Field
cards.notes: Assemble a six-person team when registration opens, or watch the relay games and the gold-helmeted official from Mac Field.
cards.short_summary: A deliberately playful field day sends six-person teams through unconventional relay games.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell says Professor Wayne Moyer helped create the Relays in 1973 as a spring celebration and spoof of other Iowa relays, traditionally starting them in a gold-painted helmet.
cards.access_notes: Participation details vary by year; follow current campus announcements before forming a team or attending Mac Field.

cards.title: See the World Take the Harris Stage
cards.subtitle: The International Student Organization’s spring showcase
cards.notes: Look for the spring program and arrive according to current event guidance; students can also follow ISO calls for performers.
cards.short_summary: Student performances transform cultural knowledge into an annual campus-stage showcase.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell documents ISO Cultural Evening as a spring series of performances organized by the International Students Organization at the Harris Center.
cards.access_notes: Check the College event calendar for the next date, audience rules, and performer sign-up information.

cards.title: Receive a Class-Year Medallion
cards.subtitle: A symbolic welcome before classes begin
cards.notes: New students should follow orientation instructions for the ceremony and keep the engraved medallion as a class keepsake.
cards.short_summary: A silver class-year medallion links arriving students to the College’s founding gift.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell describes a pre-class Medallion Ceremony where each new student receives a silver medallion engraved with their class year, symbolizing the College’s founding silver dollar.
cards.access_notes: The supporting article documents the Class of 2019 ceremony; verify the current orientation schedule before relying on its continuation.

cards.title: Dress Up for the Campus Waltz
cards.subtitle: Formal fashions and dancing, Grinnell-style
cards.notes: Watch the campus calendar for a winter or spring edition, then confirm admission details and any offered dance instruction.
cards.short_summary: Students trade everyday clothes for formal dress at seasonal waltz evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell’s official traditions page lists dressing in fine fashions for the winter or spring waltz among the College’s distinctive traditions.
cards.access_notes: No current date, admission policy, or venue is stated on the traditions page; consult the live campus calendar.

cards.title: Trace the After-Hours Bakery Run
cards.subtitle: A food outing preserved in Grinnell’s tradition list
cards.notes: Confirm the bakery’s current location, hours, transportation, and ordering rules before attempting this food-centered tradition.
cards.short_summary: The College’s own tradition list remembers a bakery trip defined by its unusually late hour.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell’s official traditions page explicitly identifies 2 a.m. bakery runs as a distinctive Grinnell tradition.
cards.access_notes: The source does not identify a bakery or verify present-day hours; do not make the trip without checking a direct business source.

cards.title: Read the Writing in Burling
cards.subtitle: A sanctioned tradition only where library policy permits
cards.notes: Observe the accumulated writing without marking other surfaces; ask library staff which areas, if any, currently permit additions.
cards.short_summary: Layers of bathroom writing form an unusual, officially acknowledged piece of library culture.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell’s official traditions page names adding to the graffiti collection covering Burling Library bathrooms as a distinctive campus practice.
cards.access_notes: Library access and marking policies are not stated on the source page; obtain staff guidance and never mark unauthorized property.

cards.title: Celebrate the Quince Someone Missed
cards.subtitle: SOL’s adaptation of a quinceañera for a senior member
cards.notes: Follow the Student Organization of Latines for current invitations and attend respectfully as a guest of the student-led celebration.
cards.short_summary: SOL honors a senior who did not have a quinceañera with a campus cultural gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell documents SOL’s tradition of hosting a Quince for a senior member who did not have a quinceañera growing up, with dance performances and Latinx food.
cards.source_title: The Student Organization of Latines: Tradition, Love, and Communidad
cards.access_notes: The article describes a 2022–23 revival plan; confirm whether SOL is hosting the event in the current academic year.

cards.title: Cook Across Cultures at Food Bazaar
cards.subtitle: An annual student-chef event organized by ISO
cards.notes: Watch ISO announcements for chef or volunteer registration, ingredient guidance, allergy information, and attendee access.
cards.short_summary: Student chefs prepare dishes from their home cultures for a large campus gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell describes the ISO Food Bazaar as an annual culinary event where student chefs cook and serve food from around the world.
cards.access_notes: The annual tradition is documented historically; consult current ISO notices for the next event, admission, and food-safety details.

cards.title: Turn One Day Scarlet
cards.subtitle: Grinnell’s annual community giving event
cards.notes: Join the annual celebration through its current campaign page; review the active challenges before choosing whether to contribute.
cards.short_summary: Students, alumni, families, faculty, and staff reconnect through a College-wide day of giving.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell states that alumni, parents, students, faculty, and staff come together every year for Scarlet & Give Back Day.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 giving day has passed; use the College’s current campaign page for the next date and participation options.

warnings: The Medallion Ceremony and SOL Quince have direct institutional documentation but their cited pages do not establish continuation during the 2026–27 academic year; access notes flag verification needs.
The 2 a.m. Bakery Run is on the College’s current traditions page, but the supporting page names neither a business nor current operating hours.
Burling Library graffiti should be observed or extended only where current library policy explicitly permits marking.
Exactly one board and ten distinct tradition cards are included; all source URLs are direct HTTPS pages.
